name: Pip the Little Lantern
premise: Pip is a small paper-lantern creature who glows a soft warm orange. Every evening Pip lights up one little thing: a sleepy animal finding its way home, five fireflies to count, why the moon follows you. Thirty seconds, no shouting, no jump cuts, made to be played at bedtime.
audience: children 2 to 6 and the parents holding the phone; parents must enjoy it enough to play it again
promise: One little light before bed, every day
anchor: Pip: a round, hand-sized paper lantern with a soft orange glow, stubby felt legs, two dot eyes and a tiny tin cap with a loop handle, bobbing gently as it walks through a storybook woodland at dusk
material: Classic bedtime routines: counting, colours, animal homes, small kindnesses, gentle why-questions; nothing from the creator's own life is needed
tone: gentle, slow, warm, a picture book read in a quiet voice
